values: Membership: Very low; allocation: High. No salmonid/anadromous compartment exists. Yellowtail represents a mobile marine fish migrating outside/into the coastal model area, giving a large pelagic/benthopelagic visitor analogue. Cold-water, anadromous/freshwater stages, family and species feeding differ; small forage and demersal source fish pools are poorer size/mobility matches. One represented candidate; 100% allocation adds no split uncertainty. Sources: SOJ-2023 main methods/Table 1; SOJ-2023 Supplement S 3/S 4; Local SAU Catch / Classic PPR; Retained primary WoRMS taxonomy.

Membership: High; allocation: High. Exact representative species in publisher Table S 3. No competing source assignment is evidenced; whole-LME transfer remains a separate model-applicability limitation. One represented candidate; 100% allocation adds no split uncertainty. Sources: SOJ-2023 main methods/Table 1; SOJ-2023 Supplement S 3/S 4; Local SAU Catch / Classic PPR; Retained primary WoRMS taxonomy.

Membership: Very low; allocation: Medium. No gadid/codling/eelpout pool exists. Use the source mobile coastal Seabass and demersal Sebastes Rockfish together as predatory shelf/benthopelagic fish analogues; both are needed because the northern/deeper target assemblage spans water-column and bottom habitats. Their families, thermal setting and habitats differ; flatfish pools require an additional body-form mismatch. Weights use complete 2013 S 4 detailed-fleet group catches (not rounded printed row totals), assumed transferable to regional landings and all 1950–2019 years/bases. Sources: SOJ-2023 main methods/Table 1; SOJ-2023 Supplement S 3/S 4; Local SAU Catch / Classic PPR; Retained primary WoRMS taxonomy.
